question: Which of the following is the only large river in the Indian desert?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Luni River**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Luni River originates from Nag Pahar or Naga hills in the Ajmer district of Rajasthan.
 
• Luni originates in the Pushkar valley of the Aravalli Range, near Ajmer and passes through the southeastern portion of the Thar Desert.
 
• It is the only large river in the Indian desert.
 
• It ends in the marshy lands of Rann of Kutch in Gujarat.
 
• Luni River flows through the Ajmer, Barmer, Jalore, Jodhpur, Nagaur, Pali, and Sirohi districts of Rajasthan and the Banaskantha and Patan districts of Gujarat.
 
• Sukri, Mithri River, Bandi, Khari, Jawai, Guhiya and Sagi are the left-bank tributary of River Luni.
 
• Jojari is the right bank tributary of River Luni.
 
• Jaswant Sagar Dam was built in 1892 by Maharaja Jaswant Singh and is one of the largest artificial lakes in India.
 
• Sardar Samand and Jawai dam are major irrigation projects on River Luni.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Betwa River

 
 
• It is also known as Betravati and Vetravati, which is a major river in India.
 
• Originates from Kumra Gao (Gohar Ganj Tehsil) of Raisen and flows into Vidisha
 
• During its total course of 590 km, the Betwa river passes through the states of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• Rivers are the lifelines of human establishments.
 
• They provide us with water and fertile lands. Civilizations have always settled on the banks of rivers.
 
• Betwa also passes through many major cities and districts including, Vidisha, Sanchi, and Orchha.
 
• It empties in the Yamuna river in Hamirpur, Uttar Pradesh.
 
 
 
• The Kosi:
 
 
• It is an antecedent river with its source to the north of Mount Everest in Tibet, where its mainstream Arun rises.
 
• After crossing the Central Himalayas in Nepal, it is joined by the Son Kosi from the West and the Tamur Kosi from the east.
 
• It forms Sapt Kosi after uniting with the river Arun.
 
 
 
• **Banas river:**
 
 
• Banas river originates from Khamnor Hills of the Aravalli Range, near Kumbhalgarh in Rajsamand, Rajasthan. '
 
• Banas river is a tributary of the Chambal River and it is approximately 512 kilometres in length.
 
• This river is also called ‘Van Ki Asha‘.
 
• There is another river in Rajasthan with the name of Banas.
 
• The Banas river entirely flows within Rajasthan in:-
 
 
• Ajmer, Bhilwara, Bundi, Chittorgarh, Dausa, Jaipur, Pali, Rajsamand, Sawai Madhopur, Sirohi, Tonk, and Udaipur districts of Rajasthan. 
 
 
 
• It flows northeast through the Mewar region of Rajasthan and meets the Chambal near the village of Rameshwar in Sawai Madhopur district.
